# nepui

> nepui is a lightweight ui component library providing accessible, customizable components for HTML/CSS/JavaScript and React.

## Documentation

* [Documentation](https://nepui.vercel.app/docs)
* [Components](https://nepui.vercel.app/docs/components)
* [CLI](https://nepui.vercel.app/docs/cli)
* [Changelog](https://nepui.vercel.app/docs/changelog)

## Components

### HTML

* [Button](https://nepui.vercel.app/docs/components/html/button): A button triggers an action, submits a form, or performs another user-initiated operation.
* [Spinner](https://nepui.vercel.app/docs/components/html/spinner): An indicator that can be used to show a loading state.
* [Label](https://nepui.vercel.app/docs/components/html/label): Renders an accessible label associated with controls.
* [Checkbox](https://nepui.vercel.app/docs/components/html/checkbox): A control that allows the user to toggle between checked and not checked.
* [Checkbox Group](https://nepui.vercel.app/docs/components/html/checkbox-group): Provides shared state to a series of checkboxes.
* [Input](https://nepui.vercel.app/docs/components/html/input): A text input component for forms and user data entry with built-in styling and accessibility features.
* [Steps](https://nepui.vercel.app/docs/components/html/steps): A multi-step process indicator that guides users through a sequence of actions or tasks.
* [Badge](https://nepui.vercel.app/docs/components/html/badge): A badge displays a short piece of information, such as a status, a label or a count.
* [Button Group](https://nepui.vercel.app/docs/components/html/button-group): A container that groups related buttons together with consistent styling.
* [Separator](https://nepui.vercel.app/docs/components/html/separator): Visually or semantically separates content.
* [Skeleton](https://nepui.vercel.app/docs/components/html/skeleton): Use to show a placeholder while content is loading.
* [Textarea](https://nepui.vercel.app/docs/components/html/textarea): Displays a form textarea or a component that looks like a textarea.
* [Field](https://nepui.vercel.app/docs/components/html/field): Combine labels, controls, and help text to compose accessible form fields and grouped inputs.
* [Kbd](https://nepui.vercel.app/docs/components/html/kbd): Used to display textual user input from keyboard.
* [Select](https://nepui.vercel.app/docs/components/html/select): Displays a list of options for the user to pick from, as a Base UI popup or as a native select.
* [Empty](https://nepui.vercel.app/docs/components/html/empty): Use the Empty component to display an empty state.
* [Accordion](https://nepui.vercel.app/docs/components/html/accordion): A vertically stacked set of interactive headings that each reveal a section of content.
* [Item](https://nepui.vercel.app/docs/components/html/item): A versatile component for displaying content with media, title, description, and actions.
* [Marker](https://nepui.vercel.app/docs/components/html/marker): Displays an inline status, system note, bordered row, or labeled separator in a conversation.
* [Popover](https://nepui.vercel.app/docs/components/html/popover): Displays rich content in a portal, triggered by a button.
* [Breadcrumb](https://nepui.vercel.app/docs/components/html/breadcrumb): Displays the path to the current resource using a hierarchy of links.
* [Tooltip](https://nepui.vercel.app/docs/components/html/tooltip): A popup that displays information related to an element when the element receives keyboard focus or the mouse hovers over it.
* [Table](https://nepui.vercel.app/docs/components/html/table): A responsive table component.
* [Tabs](https://nepui.vercel.app/docs/components/html/tabs): A set of layered sections of content, known as tab panels, that are displayed one at a time.
* [OTP Field](https://nepui.vercel.app/docs/components/html/otp-field): A segmented input for one-time passwords and verification codes.
* [Menu](https://nepui.vercel.app/docs/components/html/menu): Displays a menu to the user — such as a set of actions or functions — triggered by a button.
* [Radio Group](https://nepui.vercel.app/docs/components/html/radio-group): A set of checkable buttons—known as radio buttons—where no more than one of the buttons can be checked at a time
* [Switch](https://nepui.vercel.app/docs/components/html/switch): A control that allows the user to toggle between checked and not checked.
* [Meter](https://nepui.vercel.app/docs/components/html/meter): A graphical display of a numeric value within a range.
* [Progress](https://nepui.vercel.app/docs/components/html/progress): Displays an indicator showing the completion progress of a task, typically displayed as a progress bar.
* [Slider](https://nepui.vercel.app/docs/components/html/slider): An input where the user selects a value from within a given range.
* [Alert](https://nepui.vercel.app/docs/components/html/alert): Displays a callout for user attention.
* [Aspect Ratio](https://nepui.vercel.app/docs/components/html/aspect-ratio): Displays content within a desired ratio.
* [Avatar](https://nepui.vercel.app/docs/components/html/avatar): An image element with a fallback for representing the user.
* [Toggle](https://nepui.vercel.app/docs/components/html/toggle): A two-state button that can be either on or off.
* [Typeset](https://nepui.vercel.app/docs/components/html/typeset): A styling system for HTML and rendered markdown, from blog posts to streaming chat. One CSS file you own.
* [Card](https://nepui.vercel.app/docs/components/html/card): Displays a card with header, content, and footer.
* [Collapsible](https://nepui.vercel.app/docs/components/html/collapsible): An interactive component which expands/collapses a panel.
* [Toggle Group](https://nepui.vercel.app/docs/components/html/toggle-group): A set of two-state buttons that can be toggled on or off.
* [Scroll Area](https://nepui.vercel.app/docs/components/html/scroll-area): Augments native scroll functionality for custom, cross-browser styling.
* [Input Group](https://nepui.vercel.app/docs/components/html/input-group): Add addons, buttons, and helper content to inputs.

## Supported Targets

* HTML — Components use HTML, CSS, and JavaScript where required.
* React — Components are provided as React components with TypeScript and CSS.

## Installation

### HTML

HTML components can be copied directly from their documentation or fetched from the HTML registry.

```bash
npx nepui add button --target html
npx nepui add spinner --target html
```

### React

React components can be added using the nepui CLI.

```bash
npx nepui add button --target react
npx nepui add spinner --target react
```

## Registry

The component registry provides machine-readable component definitions.

* HTML registry index: `https://nepui.vercel.app/r/html/registry.json`
* React registry index: `https://nepui.vercel.app/r/react/registry.json`

* HTML registry: `https://nepui.vercel.app/r/html/<component>.json`
* React registry: `https://nepui.vercel.app/r/react/<component>.json`


## CLI

Use the nepui CLI to initialize a project, add component source files, and list available components. No separate install step is required; run it with `npx`. The CLI requires Node.js 18 or later.

### Initialize a project

```bash
npx nepui@latest init [directory] --target <html|react>
```

Initialization creates the base token stylesheet and target-specific folder structure. React projects also install required dependencies when needed. If no directory is provided, the CLI prompts for the target and folder.

```bash
npx nepui@latest init --target react
npx nepui@latest init --target html my-app
```

React tokens are written to `components/nepui/tokens.css`; HTML tokens are written to `styles/tokens.css`.

### Add components

```bash
npx nepui@latest add <component> [<component>...] --target <html|react>
npx nepui@latest add --all --target <html|react>
```

The default target is `html`. Add one or more component names, or use `--all` to add every component for the selected target. Do not combine component names with `--all`.

```bash
npx nepui@latest add button --target react
npx nepui@latest add button card spinner --target html
npx nepui@latest add --all --target react
```

If a destination file already exists, the CLI asks whether to overwrite, skip, or cancel. Unknown component names and invalid targets fail without writing files.

### List components

```bash
npx nepui@latest list [--target <html|react>] [--json]
```

`list` also has the `ls` alias. The default target is `html`; plain output is alphabetical. `--json` prints a JSON object to stdout for piping into other tools.

```bash
npx nepui@latest ls --target react
npx nepui@latest ls --json --target html
```

Use `--version` to print the CLI version and `--help` to show help for the CLI or a subcommand.

See the [CLI documentation](https://nepui.vercel.app/docs/cli) for full usage details.
